records.title: Unknown Citizens' Day — Philippines
factsConfirmed: Unknown Citizens' Day recognizes ordinary Filipinos who contribute to the country through daily work, civic responsibility, kindness and service without receiving public fame or prestigious titles.

Commonwealth Act No. 152, enacted without executive approval on 9 November 1936, declared the second Sunday of January every year Unknown Citizens' Day to honour the rank and file of patriotic Filipino citizens.

The law's text praises people who quietly support national progress by fulfilling their obligations. Its legally defined second Sunday is movable and should not be presented as the birthday or death anniversary of a famous individual.

records.title: W.A.T.C.H. Time Consciousness and Honesty Month — Philippines
factsConfirmed: W.A.T.C.H. means We Advocate Time Consciousness and Honesty. Its Philippine programme encourages students and communities to treat punctuality, reliable public service and honesty as practical social responsibilities.
Proclamation No. 1782, signed 21 May 2009, declared June W.A.T.C.H. Month and identified JCI Senate Philippines alongside education agencies and universities as partners in the campaign.

The text asks schools and local government units to run activities every second week of June. It refers to a June month and a specific activity week, but does not explicitly say 'every year' for the month; continuing annual legal status should therefore be reviewed separately.

records.title: Women's Role in History Month — Philippines
factsConfirmed: Women's Role in History Month highlights the contributions of Filipino women across social classes, faiths and communities, including work in education, politics, social reform and voluntary organizations.
Proclamation No. 227 of 17 March 1988 called for observance throughout March and explicitly cited House Resolution No. 20, which proposed the annual history focus.

The National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women was designated secretariat; the month-long historical recognition is not identical to the separate March 8 National Women's Day established by law in 1990.

records.title: World Clean and Green Week (Philippines) — Philippines
factsConfirmed: World Clean and Green Week in the Philippines encourages communities to reduce waste, recycle materials and restore waterways, helping people connect environmental protection with practical local action.
Proclamation No. 244, signed 3 September 1993, designated September of each year National Clean-Up Month and simultaneously fixed 17–23 September every year as World Clean and Green Week.

The decree connected the programme to the international Clean Up the World movement and Philippine activities begun in 1990; the specific week and month share the 1993 act but are not the same period or independent global origins.
